text.title: How Gates Fail Open
text.summary: Six ways a gate reports pass without evaluating, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it. All six are silent by construction: the symptom is always absence.

failure.symptom: Findings counts drop to zero across a batch. Nobody investigates, because zero findings is the outcome everyone wants. Quality complaints arrive from readers instead.
failure.cause: The judge's response parser swallows its exception and returns an empty result, so a refusal, a truncation and a rate-limit message all render as "nothing wrong".
failure.prevention: Give the gate an ERROR verdict and route it to FAIL. Our instance: `llm-judge.py:175` returns `[]` on `JSONDecodeError` and the process exits 0.

failure.symptom: Structured outputs are enabled, the parse errors disappear, and the gate still never fires.
failure.cause: Only the PARSE door was closed. A schema-valid empty array is still empty, and EMPTY was never enumerated as a mode.
failure.prevention: Enumerate all five modes. A response that validates against the schema and carries no verdict is an ERROR, not a pass — and it is the mode that survives every schema migration.

failure.symptom: The aggregate check is green for months. Individual validators, run by hand, are red.
failure.cause: Sub-checks were piped through `tee`/`tail` and their exit status discarded; the runner's own last statement was an `echo`.
failure.prevention: Accumulate statuses explicitly and exit on the accumulator. Our instance: `f066-validate-all.sh` runs six corpus validators and always exits 0.

failure.symptom: A reviewer reads the repo, sees the tool's config file, and records the risk as mitigated. No output from that tool exists anywhere in CI logs.
failure.cause: The tool was installed and configured; no runner ever calls it.
failure.prevention: Require an invocation line per checker in the contract and assert config-to-runner reachability in a rung-1 validator. Our instance: `.vale.ini` is configured and `vale` is never invoked.

failure.symptom: A correct fail-closed patch sits in review for weeks, then is abandoned as "too invasive".
failure.cause: The fix raised an exception on the ERROR path, which changed the contract of every caller, batch driver and retry wrapper downstream.
failure.prevention: Emit a synthetic high-severity finding into the channel the gate already has. The existing threshold trips; no caller changes; the diagnosis lands in the report the operator already reads.

failure.symptom: The gate is commented out of CI, or everyone has learned the bypass flag, and nobody remembers when.
failure.cause: Fail-closed was implemented with no override, so a provider outage or a flaky dependency turned the gate into an obstacle rather than a signal.
failure.prevention: Ship one named, logged, expiring hatch. A dated `--allow-degraded` in the log is a decision; a commented-out CI step is an amnesia.
